dedupe_keys.name: silent cities acoustic measurements from urban soundscapes during the covid 19 pandemic

description: A worldwide collection of urban soundscape recordings made from March to October 2020 to document how city sound changed under COVID-19 confinement. The Silent Cities project brought together 261 contributors from 35 countries, who placed programmable recorders such as AudioMoth and Song Meter SM4 in urban areas. The dataset holds the recordings as FLAC files together with CSV tables of contributor descriptions of each area, open environmental data, confinement levels and acoustic descriptors from ecoacoustic indices and automatic sound event recognition. Around 18 percent of the 10-second segments were rejected in quality control, and the authors validated the descriptors against manually annotated subsets. Coverage: sites in 35 countries. Format and access: free on OSF; to protect privacy only 10-second files with no speech identified are openly available. Caveats: sites and recorders differ, and the article is licensed CC BY-NC-ND, so check the dataset terms. Useful for studying public space noise and lockdown effects, and pandemic scenarios for urban public life; related records are not yet linked.
